threads.thread_goal: Align on program charter, scope, and success criteria for the pilot.

messages.text: Morning all, thanks for joining this channel for the outreach pilot. I have just uploaded a first draft of the Community Outreach Program Charter to our drive, linked as Community Outreach Program Charter in A1. This should also cover most of what we need for T1. The draft sets out: objectives, scope, target groups, governance, and some initial ideas for success criteria. For scope, I have focused the pilot on vulnerable residents in two neighbourhoods where we already have some presence, with activities mainly around information sessions, drop-in support, and small community events. Before we move further on staffing, events, and data, I would like your feedback on two points: 1) Are the target community segments in A1 the right starting point for a 21-day pilot, given our constraints 2) From your perspective, what are the top three metrics we should treat as our headline measures of success, so that T5 can build on them I would appreciate initial reactions today so we can iterate quickly and keep the pilot on track.

Thanks for kicking this off. I have read through A1 and mapped it loosely against the 21-day window. From a coordination angle for T11, keeping the pilot to the two neighbourhoods you propose seems realistic, especially given the staffing and training we still need to organise. One question: in the scope section you mention both one-to-many events and one-to-one support. For the first 21 days, do you see one-to-one support as scheduled slots during events only, or also separate home or office visits If we narrow that, it will help me plan dependencies with T3, T6, and T9.

I have gone through the scope and target groups in A1 as well. From an events perspective for T3, focusing on the two neighbourhoods makes sense, and I would suggest we keep the first three activities as structured events in community venues rather than spreading ourselves across too many formats. That will also make it easier later for T9 and for using A3 and A7. On the target segments, you list older adults living alone, low-income families, and recent migrants. For the pilot, could we prioritise two of these as primary audiences and treat the third as secondary That would help me design clearer event concepts and messaging.

I like the way A1 frames the objectives around both immediate support and longer-term engagement. For staffing and recruitment planning in T2 and T8, it would help if we are explicit about the primary target groups. My suggestion, based on our existing contacts, is to treat older adults living alone and low-income families as the main focus for the pilot, with recent migrants included where they overlap with those groups. That should also make it easier to brief volunteers and staff on who we are trying to reach. On metrics, I would propose: 1) number of unique residents engaged across all pilot activities, 2) proportion of participants from the defined vulnerable groups, and 3) a simple satisfaction or perceived usefulness rating collected at events. These feel measurable within our current capacity and can feed directly into T5.

I agree those three groups in A1 are important. For T5, I can definitely build on the three metrics you suggest. I just want to check a couple of details so that A4 is practical. For the first metric, do we want to count unique residents per event or across the whole pilot I can do either, but across the pilot will require a simple way to recognise returning participants. For the satisfaction rating, are we comfortable with a very short paper form at the end of each event, or do we need something more detailed I am conscious of the 21-day timeline and the need to keep data collection light for T10.

On the one-to-one support question: for the pilot, I suggest we limit this to scheduled slots during or immediately around the events, rather than separate home visits. That keeps the operational load manageable for T6 and T9 and fits our budget constraint. We can note home visits as a potential extension in a later phase. On target groups, I am leaning toward what was proposed: older adults living alone and low-income families as primary, with recent migrants as a cross-cutting group where relevant. If no one objects today, I will update A1 accordingly so that T1 can move to approval.

I have read through A1 with a communications lens, thinking ahead to A6 and T7. Narrowing to the two neighbourhoods and the two primary groups will help us craft clearer messages and choose the right channels. For success metrics, in addition to the three already mentioned, would it be useful to track how people heard about us That could be a simple tick-box on the same form that the statistician mentioned, and it would help us refine the communication plan without adding much extra work.

For counting participants, I would suggest we track both per event and across the pilot, but we can keep the method simple. Maybe we can use initials and year of birth on the sign-in sheet so we can spot duplicates without collecting unnecessary personal data. That should still respect privacy and safeguarding requirements. For the satisfaction rating, a one-question scale plus an open comment box on a short paper form should be enough. We can always refine later if the pilot shows we need more detail.

I like the idea of adding a question on how people heard about us. From a coordination point of view, that will also help us see which channels to prioritise in the timeline for T11 and in the communication plan for T7. As long as we keep it to a short list of options, it should not slow down check-in at events.

Thanks, that helps. I will design A4 so that the three headline metrics are: 1) total unique residents engaged across the pilot, with a breakdown per event, 2) proportion of participants from the two primary vulnerable groups, and 3) average satisfaction rating per event. I will also include an optional indicator on communication channels used, based on the tick-box you suggested. For T10, I will keep the data collection tools to a one-page sign-in and a one-page feedback form, and I will bring a draft to this channel before finalising.

Limiting one-to-one support to time around the events works well for planning T3 and T9. I will design the first three events so that there is a clear section in the run-of-show for short individual conversations, and I will coordinate with HR on how many staff or volunteers we need on site for that. Keeping the primary focus on older adults and low-income families will also help us choose venues that are familiar and accessible to them.

Given the feedback so far, I propose we lock in the following for the pilot scope in A1: 1) Geographic focus on the two neighbourhoods listed in the draft. 2) Primary target groups: older adults living alone and low-income families, with recent migrants included where they overlap. 3) Activity types limited to small community events with built-in one-to-one support slots, no separate home visits in this phase. Unless there are strong objections by end of day, I will treat this as agreed and update A1 so that T1 can be marked complete from a scope perspective.

On success metrics, I am comfortable confirming the three headline measures you outlined, with the communication channel question as a supporting data point. To restate them clearly for A4 and T5: 1) total unique residents engaged across the pilot, with per-event breakdown, 2) proportion of participants from the two primary vulnerable groups, and 3) average satisfaction rating per event based on a simple one-question scale. Please proceed on that basis and flag any issues with data protection or practicality as you finalise the framework.

No objections from my side. The clarified scope and target groups in A1 work well for T2 and T8. I will reflect the focus on older adults and low-income families in the role descriptions and onboarding materials, and I will make sure the sign-in and feedback forms align with the data points agreed for A4.

From a timeline view, confirming these three metrics now is very helpful. I will incorporate them into the milestone overview for T11 so that we can see where data collection and review points sit relative to the events and the pilot end date.

Thanks everyone for the quick input. To summarise where we have landed for this thread: 1) Scope in A1 is now focused on two neighbourhoods, with activities limited to small community events that include short one-to-one support slots on site. 2) Primary target groups are older adults living alone and low-income families, with recent migrants included where they overlap. 3) Our three headline success metrics for A4 and T5 are total unique residents engaged (with per-event breakdown), proportion from the primary vulnerable groups, and average satisfaction rating per event, plus an optional question on how people heard about us. I will update A1 today and share the link here so that T1 can move to formal approval with executive leadership.

threads.thread_goal: Define staffing, volunteer needs, and onboarding approach.

messages.text: Hi all, following the scope decisions in A1, I have uploaded a first draft of the Staffing and Volunteer Recruitment Plan as A2. This is my initial pass at T2 and T8. In A2 you will see: 1) a list of roles for the pilot (core staff, event leads, volunteer roles), 2) estimated time commitments for each, and 3) proposed recruitment channels and timelines. I have also sketched a draft volunteer onboarding and training flow that will later be formalised into A5. To move forward, I need your input on two things: a) the number and type of volunteers we need for the first three events, and b) whether the onboarding steps and training topics I propose for A5 cover the essentials, especially around safeguarding and privacy. Please add comments or respond here so we can refine this quickly.

Thanks for sharing A2. Looking at the event layout I have in mind for T3 and T9, I think we need a minimum of: 1) one event lead, 2) one person focused on registration and sign-in, 3) two to three volunteers for general support and one-to-one conversations, and 4) one person keeping an eye on logistics and safety. Some of these roles can be combined if we have experienced people. For the first three events, I would suggest we plan for four to five volunteers per event, plus core staff. That gives us enough coverage if someone is ill or if turnout is higher than expected.

I have reviewed A2 alongside the draft timeline for T11. Given the 21-day window, I agree with the event manager that four to five volunteers per event is a good target. It also gives us some flexibility if we need to split tasks like registration and feedback collection. From a coordination point of view, it would help if we can confirm a pool of around ten volunteers for the pilot, so we can rotate them across the three events without overloading anyone.

I have skimmed A2 and the onboarding outline for A5. The overall structure looks sound. On numbers, I am comfortable aiming for a pool of around ten volunteers, as suggested, with four to five per event. We just need to be realistic about how quickly we can recruit and brief them within the 21 days. On training topics, I want to be sure we are explicit about safeguarding, privacy, and how to handle any disclosures of risk or distress. If we are not fully confident on any of those points, we should bring in someone from our safeguarding team to review A5 before we roll it out.

From the data side, I would like to make sure the onboarding in A5 includes a short section on how volunteers should handle sign-in sheets and feedback forms for T10. For example, not leaving forms unattended, keeping them in a folder, and handing them to the designated data person at the end of the event. It might also help to include a simple script so volunteers know how to explain why we are collecting data and that participation is voluntary.

Looking at A2 with a communications hat on, I think the recruitment channels you list are a good start. We might also want to tap into local community groups and libraries in the two neighbourhoods, since they often have noticeboards and mailing lists. If we do that, I can help draft a short volunteer call-out that aligns with the tone we will use in T7 and the events calendar in A6.

Thanks for the detailed breakdown. Based on your input and the management assistant's suggestion, I will update A2 to reflect a target of ten volunteers in the pool, with four to five scheduled per event. I will also clarify the roles you listed so that we can match people to tasks more easily. For T2, I will adjust the recruitment timeline to make sure we have at least a core group confirmed before the first event date is locked in under T9.

Good point on data handling. I will add a short section to the onboarding flow in A5 covering: how to manage sign-in and feedback forms, who to hand them to, and a simple explanation volunteers can use when asking participants to complete them. I will coordinate with you to make sure the wording matches what you need for T10 and A4.

On training topics, the current draft of A5 includes: introduction to the program and target groups, communication basics, boundaries and when to escalate concerns, safeguarding principles, privacy and data handling, and practical event logistics. I agree we should have our safeguarding lead review the safeguarding and incident response parts before we finalise. I will mark those sections in A5 and send them to the safeguarding team for a quick check.

Once you update A2 with the confirmed volunteer numbers and roles, I will plug that into the overall plan for T11 so we can see where we might have gaps. It would be helpful if you can also flag any roles that must be filled by staff rather than volunteers, so we do not over-rely on volunteers for critical safeguarding decisions.

For the onboarding flow in A5, could we also include a short walk-through of the event run-of-show from A3 and A7 I find that volunteers feel more confident when they can see how their tasks fit into the overall sequence. We could do this as a simple visual or checklist during the briefing.

Given the alignment so far, I propose we formally agree on the volunteer numbers for the first three events: a pool of around ten volunteers for the pilot, with four to five volunteers scheduled per event, covering registration, general support, and one-to-one conversations, alongside core staff. I will reflect this in A2 and use it as the basis for recruitment under T2.

I support that proposal. Let us lock in the pool of ten volunteers with four to five per event as our working assumption for the pilot. If recruitment falls short, we can adjust event formats rather than stretching people too thin.

On the onboarding and training content in A5, the structure you describe covers the key areas I was concerned about. Provided the safeguarding team signs off on the safeguarding and incident response sections, I am happy for us to adopt this onboarding flow and topic list for the pilot. Please treat that review as a condition before we roll it out to volunteers.

To wrap this up from my side: 1) I will finalise A2 with a target pool of ten volunteers and four to five per event, plus clarified role descriptions. 2) I will update A5 to include the data handling guidance, a short run-of-show overview, and the agreed training topics, then send the safeguarding sections for review. Once we have that sign-off, we can start scheduling onboarding sessions in line with the event dates under T9.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in the design and logistics for the first outreach event.

messages.text: Hi team, I have drafted the concept and logistics for our first outreach event and added them to the shared folder. The run-of-show and checklist are captured in the Single Event Logistics and Risk Checklist A7, and I have aligned the steps with the Outreach Events Operating Procedures in A3. This is my current work on T3 and T9. Summary of the proposal: 1) Format: community information and support session with small group activities and short one-to-one conversations. 2) Location: community hall in one of the two pilot neighbourhoods, accessible by public transport and step-free. 3) Timing: weekday late afternoon to early evening, to suit both older adults and families. 4) Built-in slots for registration, welcome, group activity, one-to-one support, and closing. I have suggested two possible dates in the week starting 10 days from now. Before we lock anything, I need your views on the date, time, and location, and whether the minimum staffing in A7 feels realistic given the volunteer plan in A2.

Thanks for putting this together. Looking at your proposed dates against the draft timeline for T11, the community hall slot on the Wednesday of that week seems to give us a bit more breathing room for volunteer onboarding and communications than the Monday option. It also leaves space for a short debrief before the second event. On timing, a late afternoon start with an early evening finish fits well with the constraints we have captured so far.

From the staffing side, the minimum numbers in A7 line up with what we agreed in A2: one event lead, one person on registration, two to three volunteers for support, and someone watching logistics and safety. If we go with the Wednesday date, I am confident we can have at least a core group of volunteers onboarded in time, assuming we start outreach this week. I would just suggest we avoid scheduling the event too late in the evening, as that can be harder for older adults.

I have reviewed the concept in A7 and the alignment with A3. The community hall you propose is in one of our focus neighbourhoods and meets our accessibility requirements, so I am comfortable with that choice. I also like the structure of the run-of-show, especially the clear slots for one-to-one support. My main question is whether we can realistically manage both group activities and individual conversations with the staffing we have, or whether we should simplify the group part for the first event.

From a communications angle, the Wednesday late afternoon slot at the community hall works well. It is a familiar venue for local residents, and we can highlight that in the promotion materials for T7 and the events calendar in A6. If we confirm the date and time soon, I can start drafting flyers and online posts that match the event concept you have outlined.

For T10, the run-of-show in A7 gives me clear points where we can collect data without disrupting the flow. I suggest we do sign-in at the start, a short satisfaction form near the end, and, if needed, a quick headcount during the group activity. It would help if we can assign one person specifically to data tasks at each event, so that volunteers know who to hand forms to.

That is a fair question. For the first event, we can keep the group activity simple, for example a short discussion circle with prompts about local needs, rather than anything complex. The one-to-one conversations can then focus on more personal questions. With four to five volunteers plus staff, I believe this is manageable, especially if we clearly assign who leads the group part and who focuses on individual support. I can adjust A7 to make those roles explicit.

Assigning a specific data person per event makes sense. We can reflect that in both A7 and the staffing overview in A2. I will also note it in the project timeline under T11 so that we remember to brief that person before each event.

I can identify one volunteer or staff member per event to act as the data point person, and I will include that in the role descriptions in A2 and the onboarding content in A5. That way, everyone knows who is responsible for sign-in sheets and feedback forms on the day.

Based on the feedback, I propose we confirm: 1) the community hall in the first pilot neighbourhood as the location, 2) the Wednesday date in the week we discussed, and 3) a time slot of 4pm to 6.30pm. This should work for both older adults and families, and it gives us enough time for registration, a simple group activity, and one-to-one conversations. I will update A7 and the draft in A6 accordingly if we agree.

I am happy to confirm that proposal. Let us lock in the community hall in the first pilot neighbourhood, on the Wednesday of that week, from 4pm to 6.30pm, as the date, time, and location for the first outreach event. Please proceed with booking and logistics on that basis.

On the run-of-show and staffing, I support your suggestion to keep the group activity simple and to assign clear roles for group facilitation, one-to-one support, registration, logistics, and data. With four to five volunteers plus staff, that feels manageable. Let us treat the minimum staffing in A7 as our baseline for the pilot, and we can adjust if we see that we consistently need more or fewer people.

Great, with the date, time, and location confirmed, I will update A6 and start drafting the communication materials for T7. I will share a short event description and key messages here for review before we publish anything.

With the run-of-show and staffing now clearer, I will adjust the data collection plan in A4 and T10 to match the confirmed timing. I will assume sign-in from 4pm, group activity around the middle, and feedback forms in the last 15 minutes, and I will note the data point person role explicitly.

To close the loop from a coordination perspective: 1) I will update the project timeline in T11 with the confirmed date, time, and location, plus key milestones for communications, volunteer onboarding, and logistics checks. 2) I will also make sure the risk and contingency items in A7 are reflected in our overall risk view, so we can track any issues that might affect the launch.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on monitoring, evaluation, and data collection processes.

messages.text: Hello everyone, I have uploaded a first draft of the Monitoring and Evaluation Framework as A4. This is my current work on T5 and the basis for T10. The framework lists proposed indicators, data sources, collection frequency, and responsibilities. It reflects the three headline metrics we agreed in TH1: total unique residents engaged, proportion from the primary vulnerable groups, and average satisfaction rating per event, plus an optional question on how people heard about us. I have also suggested some additional indicators, such as number of referrals made to other services. Before we finalise A4, I would like your feedback on: 1) whether the list of indicators is the right size for a 21-day pilot, 2) how often we should review the data during the pilot, and 3) who should be responsible for capturing data at each event and for maintaining the central data file.

Thanks for pulling A4 together. At first glance, the three headline metrics look well captured. I am slightly concerned that the additional indicators might be too ambitious for a short pilot, especially if they require extra forms or follow-up. I would prefer we keep the list tight and focus on what we can reliably collect at each event without overloading staff and volunteers. On review frequency, I would like us to have at least one mid-pilot check-in on the data, plus a final review at the end.

I agree with keeping the indicator list manageable. For volunteers and staff, the simpler the better. The three main metrics plus the communication channel question feel realistic. The referrals indicator is useful, but maybe we can track it in a very simple way, for example a tally kept by the event lead, rather than a separate form. On responsibilities, I suggest we assign one data point person per event, as discussed in TH3, and have you maintain the central data file in A4.

From the event side, the indicators you have in A4 are workable as long as we keep data collection tied closely to the run-of-show in A7. I like the idea of tracking referrals, but I would not want that to slow down conversations. A simple tick-box on the event lead's copy of the checklist in A7 could be enough. For who captures data, I support the idea that one person per event is the main contact, with volunteers helping with sign-in and forms.

Looking at A4 alongside the overall plan for T11, I would recommend we keep the indicator set to the three headline metrics plus the optional communication channel question and a simple referrals tally. That should be enough to inform the mid-pilot review and final debrief without creating a heavy reporting burden. For review frequency, a quick data check after each event plus a more structured mid-pilot review should give us enough insight to adjust if needed.

From a communications perspective, the communication channel question in A4 is particularly valuable. It will help us see which promotion efforts under T7 and A6 are working. I do not think we need many more indicators for this pilot, as long as we can break down participation by event and by target group.

Understood. I can trim A4 so that the core indicators are: 1) total unique residents engaged, with per-event counts, 2) proportion from the primary vulnerable groups, 3) average satisfaction rating per event, 4) how participants heard about us, and 5) a simple tally of referrals made to other services. I will remove the more detailed outcome indicators for now and note them as ideas for a later phase. For review frequency, I can prepare a short summary after each event and a slightly more detailed snapshot for the mid-pilot review.

On responsibilities, I can make sure that for each event we nominate a data point person in the staffing plan in A2 and in the onboarding materials in A5. That person can be either a staff member or a well-briefed volunteer, but they should know they are accountable for collecting and handing over the forms to you.

For the event-level process in T10, could you add a simple step-by-step in A4 that we can mirror in A7 For example: 1) data point person collects sign-in sheets at the end of registration, 2) volunteers hand completed feedback forms to the data person, 3) data person checks counts against headcount before leaving the venue. That will help keep things consistent across events.

Yes, I can add that step-by-step process to A4 and coordinate with you so that A7 reflects the same sequence. I will also include a note on where the completed forms should be stored centrally and who has access, to stay aligned with privacy requirements.

Given the adjustments you propose, I am comfortable confirming the final list of indicators for the pilot as you outlined: the three headline metrics, the communication channel question, and a simple referrals tally. Let us treat that as the agreed scope for A4 and T5. Please keep the framework as light as possible while still allowing us to tell a clear story at the end of the pilot.

On responsibilities for data capture, I would like to formalise what has been suggested: each event will have a designated data point person responsible for sign-in and feedback forms, supported by volunteers, and you as statistician will maintain the central data file and produce short summaries after each event and at mid-pilot. If everyone is comfortable with that, we can document it in A4 and T10.
That division of responsibilities works for me. I will reflect it in the overall plan for T11 so that we can see clearly who is doing what at each event and when the data summaries are due.

Thanks for all the input. I will now: 1) update A4 to reflect the agreed indicator list and the event-level data process, 2) document the responsibilities for data point persons and for maintaining the central file, and 3) set up a simple template for post-event and mid-pilot summaries under T10. I will share the updated A4 in this channel once it is ready.

threads.thread_goal: Set up operational processes, knowledge hub, and overall timeline.

messages.text: Hi everyone, I have pulled together a first draft of the standard operating procedures for events and visits in A3, and a simple index for our central knowledge hub in A8. This is part of my work on T4, T6, T11, and it will also support T12. In A3 you will find draft processes and checklists for pre-event, during-event, and post-event tasks, aligned with A7. In A8 I have outlined a folder structure and naming conventions for key documents like A1, A2, A4, A5, A6, and A7. I would like your feedback on two points: 1) whether the proposed knowledge hub structure and access rules in A8 work for you, and 2) whether the SOPs in A3 cover the main operational and risk management steps we need for the pilot. Once we agree, I will finalise the timeline in T11 and prepare inputs for the internal launch briefing under T12.

Thanks for consolidating this. The structure in A8 looks logical to me, with separate folders for governance, staffing, events, data, and communications. For access, my instinct is to give all core team members in this channel read and edit access to the main folders, with more restricted access only for any sensitive HR or incident reports. We should avoid creating too many barriers, otherwise people will start saving files elsewhere.

I have looked at A8 with a focus on how people will find documents quickly. The folder structure is clear, and the naming conventions will help. I would suggest we add a short 'Start here' note in A8 that points to the most important documents for new team members, such as A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, and A7. I can also help draft a short usage guide once the structure is agreed, as required under T4.

From an HR and onboarding perspective, the SOPs in A3 cover the main steps I would expect before, during, and after events, including briefings, debriefings, and incident reporting. I would just like to make sure that any documents containing personal data or sensitive notes are clearly flagged in A8 and that access is limited to those who need it. For example, detailed incident reports or HR records should not be in the same open folder as general event materials.

On the operational side, A3 and A7 together give a good overview of what needs to happen around each event. I appreciate the clear pre-event checklist, especially the sections on venue checks and materials. For the pilot, I think this level of detail is enough, as long as we keep the checklists to one or two pages so they are usable on the day.

From the data perspective, I would like to confirm that the data folder in A8 will contain A4, the data collection templates, and the central data file for T10, with access limited to this core team and any necessary support staff. That should help us manage privacy while still allowing collaboration. It might also be useful to include a short note in A3 about where completed forms should be stored after each event.

Good point on sensitive documents. In A8, I can create a clearly marked restricted folder for HR and incident-related materials, with access limited to HR, the CEO, and myself. All general event materials, checklists, and communications can stay in the main shared folders. I will also add a note in A3 to remind people not to store detailed personal information in the general event folders.

With those adjustments, I am comfortable agreeing the overall structure and access approach for the knowledge hub in A8: shared access for this core team to the main folders, with a restricted area for HR and incident materials. Let us adopt that as our standard for the pilot so that everyone knows where to find the latest versions of A1 through A7.

On the SOPs in A3, I will incorporate the data storage note from the statistician and the reminder about sensitive information. I will also keep the checklists concise so they are practical in the field. Once that is done, I will share a short summary in this channel so everyone knows where to look in A3 and A7 for their tasks.

Once the structure in A8 is final, I will draft the short usage guide required for T4, including the 'Start here' note and a quick overview of where to find A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, and A7. I will also include a reminder about the restricted folder for sensitive materials.

Turning to the overall timeline in T11, I have mapped out key milestones: 1) finalising A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, and A8 in the next few days, 2) confirming the first event logistics under T9, 3) completing initial volunteer onboarding under T8 before the first event, 4) running the three events within the 21-day window, and 5) preparing the internal launch briefing under T12. I have also highlighted risks to the launch date, mainly around delays in approvals or volunteer recruitment.

The timeline you describe for T11 looks aligned with our 21-day constraint. I would like us to formally confirm it as the working plan for the pilot, with the understanding that we will adjust if major risks materialise. Once you have the visual timeline ready, please share it in this channel and I will use it as a basis for the internal launch briefing under T12.

From my side, the milestones for volunteer recruitment and onboarding in T2 and T8 fit within that timeline, as long as we start outreach immediately. I will keep you posted if we see any risk of not reaching the target pool of volunteers in time.

The event-related milestones in T3 and T9 also look achievable with the confirmed date for the first event. I will coordinate with you to make sure the logistics checks in A7 line up with the dates in the timeline.

To summarise this thread: 1) We have agreed on the knowledge hub structure and access rules in A8, with shared access for this core team and a restricted folder for HR and incident materials. 2) The SOPs in A3, aligned with A7, will guide pre-event, during-event, and post-event tasks, with concise checklists and clear notes on data storage and sensitive information. 3) The high-level timeline in T11, covering finalisation of key artifacts, event logistics, volunteer onboarding, the three events, and the internal briefing under T12, is confirmed as our working plan for the 21-day pilot. I will rely on this structure and timeline when preparing the internal launch briefing.
